test_title: PYST 60: RRB Group D - GA (Held On: 23 Dec, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Which Ministry of the Government of India carried out the Management Effectiveness Evaluation (MEE) for 2020-2025?

options.text: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change

solution:
The correct answer is __**Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC)** is the nodal agency in the administrative structure of the Central Government for the planning, promotion, coordination, and overseeing the implementation of India's environmental and forestry policies and programmes.
 
• The **Management Effectiveness Evaluation (MEE)** for the cycle **2020-2025** represents the **5th cycle** of assessment for **National Parks** and **Wildlife Sanctuaries** in India.
 
• This evaluation process is conducted by the **MoEFCC** with technical support from the **Wildlife Institute of India (WII)**, an autonomous institution based in **Dehradun**.
 
• The primary objective of **MEE** is to assess how well **Protected Areas** are being managed and whether they are achieving the goals for which they were established.
 
• For the **2020-2025** cycle, the evaluation framework involves a set of **30 indicators** categorized under six elements: **Context, Planning, Inputs, Process, Outputs, and Outcomes**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Management Effectiveness Evaluation (MEE):**
 
 
• It is a global tool adopted from the **IUCN World Commission on Protected Areas (WCPA)** framework to evaluate the management efficiency of conservation sites.
 
• India is one of the few countries in the world that has institutionalized the **MEE** process for its network of **Protected Areas** since **2006**.
 
• The evaluation helps in identifying gaps in management and provides a roadmap for future conservation strategies at both the state and national levels.
 
 
 
• **Wildlife Institute of India (WII):**
 
 
• Established in **1982**, **WII** provides scientific knowledge and personnel for the conservation of wildlife in the country.
 
• It plays a critical role in developing the **MEE** scorecard and training the independent expert committees that visit the field sites for data collection.
 
 
 
• **Tiger Reserves and MEE-TR:**
 
 
• Apart from general Protected Areas, the **National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA)** also carries out a separate **Management Effectiveness Evaluation of Tiger Reserves (MEE-TR)** every four years.
 
• The **MEE** of **Tiger Reserves** follows a similar methodology but focuses specifically on the **54 Tiger Reserves** currently present in India.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Rating Scale:** The sites evaluated under **MEE** are given scores and categorized into four ratings: **Very Good** (75% and above), **Good** (60-74%), **Satisfactory** (50-59%), and **Poor** (less than 50%).
 
• **MEE of Zoos (MEE-ZOO):** Recently, the **MoEFCC** also extended this evaluation framework to **Zoos** in India, aiming to improve the standards of animal housing, healthcare, and conservation breeding.
 
• **Data Facts:** India has a network of over **900 Protected Areas**, including **106 National Parks** and **573 Wildlife Sanctuaries**. The **5th cycle** aims to provide a comprehensive look at the health of these ecosystems following the **Wildlife (Protection) Amendment Act, 2022**.
 
• **Global Commitments:** These evaluations assist India in meeting its international obligations under the **Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD)** and the **Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework**.
